'Effective number of members': how many equal positions would be as concentrated (1 / sum of squared weights). 'Members that make half': the largest members needed to add up to 50%. 'Risk in the largest 3': share of the variance of the index that comes from them, with the weights of that day and the daily returns of the 504 trading days before it. DR: diversification ratio (weighted average volatility of the members divided by the volatility of the portfolio), same window. Sectors: GICS names of the fund (SMI, FTSE 100) and of Yahoo Finance (KOSPI).

Members are ranked by their weight today. 'Part of the difference': each day, (weight in equal weight minus weight in the index, the day before) times the return of the member, added up over the group and averaged over the period (times 252). The groups add up to the average daily return of equal weight minus that of the index weights, before costs; it is an average of daily differences, close to but not the same as the difference between compound returns.

| KOSPI | Last 1 year | 106.4% | 106.1% | +0.3 | 1.0% | 1.000 |
| KOSPI | Last 3 years | 43.4% | 43.6% | -0.3 | 1.0% | 1.000 |
| KOSPI | Last 5 years | 17.9% | 18.0% | -0.1 | 2.4% | 0.997 |
| KOSPI | Last 10 years | 12.9% | 13.2% | -0.3 | 3.1% | 0.992 |

Both without dividends, return per year. The real index held the members of each day, including the companies that have since left it. Today's members are, by construction, the ones that did well enough to be in the index now, so the gap is the survivorship bias of the index-weights portfolio (plus the changes in the number of shares, which it ignores). Over one year the gap should be close to 0: it checks that the members and weights are right.

### What holding today's weights all along would have shown

| Index | Index weights (weights move with prices) | Today's weights held all along | Equal weight | Weight of the largest 3 at the start | today |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SMI | 9.5% | 12.2% | 13.5% | 64.2% | 46.3% |
| FTSE 100 | 9.3% | 14.5% | 12.5% | 20.9% | 25.7% |
| KOSPI | 15.2% | 34.3% | 7.5% | 19.2% | 55.6% |

Return per year. 'Today's weights held all along' puts the portfolio back to the weights of 2026-09-30 every quarter. Those weights are the result of the ten years (the companies that rose the most weigh the most today), so that portfolio knows the future. It is shown only to measure how much that mistake would be worth.
